lesson.child_mission: Millimetres measure short lengths (10 mm = 1 cm). Kilometres measure long distances (1000 m = 1 km). Match the unit to the size.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Choose mm, cm, m or km: thickness of a coin; length of a pencil; length of a classroom; distance between towns. Convert 40 mm to cm.

FEEDBACK
mm; cm; m; km. 40 mm = 4 cm.

WATCH FOR
Using kilometres for a pencil length is the wrong scale.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Sort twelve everyday lengths into mm/cm/m/km. Convert six measures between mm↔cm and m↔km. Write one sentence about why unit choice matters.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.

teach_steps.explain:
Millimetres measure short lengths (10 mm = 1 cm). Kilometres measure long distances (1000 m = 1 km). Match the unit to the size.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Using kilometres for a pencil length is the wrong scale. Correct the value or method, not just the appearance of the digits.
